text:
I'm revising my earlier answer: the tenant's adverse possession most likely began in 1992, when the seven-year lease expired and he stayed on with no lease-based right to occupy, not in 1986. Stopping rent and deciding to stay did not by themselves repudiate the tenancy, and the shared note's subjective-intent test is not the usual standard, which turns on objectively hostile, open possession. Because 1992 plus 20 years runs to 2012, after the Scouts' 2009 discovery, the claim is probably not time-barred, though the outcome depends on this jurisdiction's rules on holdover tenants and repudiation.

CONFIDENCE: 45
